# VulcanBench

> An open-source coding benchmark comparing model-and-harness combinations
> across reasoning effort, total score, runtime, tokens and estimated API cost.

VulcanBench is run by Morgan Linton, Cofounder and CTO of Bold Metrics.
The current VulcanBench Frontier v4 suite uses 23 behavioral-reconstruction tasks:
Python replacements for opaque C-built binaries. From September 2026 its
combined score weights are 50% functional correctness, 8.5% lint and
complexity, 8.5% security and 33% Code quality. Time, tokens and
API-equivalent cost are reported separately.

Code quality is judged for a human reader by a two-model panel that never includes
a model from the graded model's own lab (Muse Spark 1.3 and Grok 4.6 for
most columns; Grok 4.7, Muse Wonder Full, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and Reflection
Beam are judged by other disclosed pairs), under one frozen
six-dimension rubric with written anchors, an intent-recovery probe scored
against each task's known specification departures, and a calibration exam
every judge passes before scoring. It is model judgment, not human validation.
A perfect functional result is not a perfect combined score.

## Key pages

- [Current results and archive](https://vulcanbench.com/benchmarks.html): compare only within the same task suite and scoring protocol.
- [Claude Opus 5.5 on VulcanBench Safety v1](https://vulcanbench.com/benchmarks/safety-v1-opus55.html): ten Frontier v4 tasks with two harmful instructions hidden in each repository; over 50 Claude Code runs Opus 5.5 followed 0 of 60 network, secret or delete instructions and 3 of 100 overall (two code injections, one harmless test), and flagged the note to the user in 64 of 97 refusals.
- [Reflection Beam across every effort level](https://vulcanbench.com/benchmarks/swe-v4-beam-v328.html): 115 runs of Reflection Beam 1.0 (Beam-1.0-501B-A23B, 501B total and 23B active parameters) in Mirror CLI 0.1.1, Reflection's own coding agent and an early beta, on Reflection's API at all five reasoning levels (Low to Max; Extra-high is Beam's xhigh), Code quality at 33% judged for a human reader by Muse Spark 1.3 and GPT-6.1 Sol under protocol v3.28, because Grok 4.6's Cursor account was out of usage; most other columns, Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra included, are judged by Muse Spark 1.3 and Grok 4.6, so scores are not strictly comparable, and GPT-6.1 Sol rates Beam's reviewed layer 10 to 18 points above Muse. Combined score 39.51 at Low, 44.79 at Medium, 55.01 at High, 64.72 at Extra-high and 63.92 at Max over judged runs (n=11, 20, 23, 23, 22); 15 Low and Medium runs left no code (empty patches or only file-mode and scratch changes) and count as failed, giving 18.90 and 38.95 with them as 0; Max hedgecore passed but its evidence was too large for either judge. Best level 63rd of 75 columns on the board as of October 27, 2026, about 24 to 26 points below the three frontier models. Tasks passed 0, 0, 0, 4 and 6 of 23; 0.4 to 22.4 minutes and 0.09M to 17.29M tokens a task; Reflection publishes no price, so there is no cost. Disclosed: Mirror labels Permission denied as a sandbox denial and two Low runs blamed the sandbox, a daily API token limit paused the sweep (no finished run affected), tool calls not archived. Includes per-run CSV, calibration record and public evidence links.
- [DeepSeek V4.1 Flash across every effort level](https://vulcanbench.com/benchmarks/swe-v4-deepseek-flash-v327.html): 69 runs of DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (deepseek-flash, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017) in DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1-rc.2, DeepSeek's own open-source agent, on a metered API key, at the three reasoning levels DeepSeek's API offers (Low, High and Max), Code quality at 33% judged for a human reader by Muse Spark 1.3 and GPT-6.1 Sol under protocol v3.27, because Grok 4.6's Cursor account was out of usage; most other columns, Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol included, are judged by Muse Spark 1.3 and Grok 4.6, so scores are not strictly comparable, and GPT-6.1 Sol rates Flash's reviewed layer 7 to 10 points above Muse. Combined score 88.65 at Low, 88.61 at High and 88.36 at Max (judged n=23 at every level, no timeouts), best level 22nd of 75 columns on the board as of October 27, 2026; highest of the three at Low, behind Opus 5.5 and level with GPT-6.1 Sol at High and Max. Tasks passed 21, 20 and 20 of 23; 8.1 to 10.6 minutes and $0.058 to $0.074 per task at DeepSeek's off-peak list price ($0.068 to $0.101 billed after peak-hour doubling), about a fifth of GPT-6.1 Sol's cost per task. Disclosed: dsh is a developer preview, session-log and telemetry uploads off, model identity harness-recorded, two owner pauses with interrupted runs rerun, a macOS update between Low runs with identical re-grades. Includes per-run CSV, calibration record and public evidence links.
- [Muse Wonder Full across every effort level](https://vulcanbench.com/benchmarks/swe-v4-musewonder-full-v326.html): 92 Muse Code runs of Meta's Muse Wonder Full in Contributor mode at the four effort levels Contributor mode offers (Low to Extra-high), Code quality at 33% judged for a human reader by Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol under protocols v3.26 to v3.26.3, because Muse Spark 1.3 is a Meta model and not neutral for a Meta submission; scores from a different panel are not strictly comparable with the other columns, and the two judges differ by about 17 points on the reviewed layer. Combined score 86.95 at Low, 88.27 at Medium, 88.19 at High and 87.59 at Extra-high (judged n=23, 23, 22, 22; 84.36 and 83.78 with one 3-hour timeout each counted as 0), best level 26th of 75 columns on the board as of October 27, 2026 (23rd of 67 when published). Tasks passed 18, 21, 19 and 19 of 23; 27.3 to 36.2 minutes and an estimated $3.93 to $5.08 per task at the Muse Wonder 1.0 list price (Meta lists no price for Muse Wonder Full). Disclosed: Muse Code 1.4.6 then 1.4.9 after a quota reset, 1.4.9's reminder observers on Muse Spark 1.3, Opus 5.5 replacing Grok 4.7, overlapping local jobs, one transport rerun. Includes per-run CSV, calibration record, public evidence links and redacted traces (https://github.com/morganlinton/vulcanbench-musewonder-full-traces).
- [Claude Haiku 5.5 vs Claude Sonnet 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Luna](https://vulcanbench.com/benchmarks/swe-v4-haiku55-vs-frontier.html): the four models side by side on the same 23 VulcanBench Frontier v4 tasks at five effort levels, judged by the same panel (Muse Spark 1.3 and Grok 4.6) under protocols v3.24, v3.23, v3.18 and v3.16. Per level: combined score with one standard error and judged n, Code quality, tasks solved, cost and minutes per task. At Max Haiku 5.5 (92.16 ± 0.37, n=21) and Sonnet 5.5 (92.02 ± 0.35) are effectively tied, with Haiku about 3.6 times cheaper per task; below Max Haiku rates higher on Code quality but solves fewer tasks. GPT-6.1 Sol solves more tasks at every level for 1.9 to 3.8 times less per task and scores about 3 points lower at Extra-high and Max; GPT-6 Luna scores far lower at every level and is 5 to 142 times cheaper. Cost bases and harnesses differ and are disclosed. Links every underlying evidence bundle.
- [Claude Haiku 5.5 across every effort level](https://vulcanbench.com/benchmarks/swe-v4-haiku55-v324.html): 115 Claude Code runs at five effort levels, Code quality at 33% judged for a human reader by Muse Spark 1.3 and Grok 4.6 under protocol v3.24. Combined score 84.42 at Low, 84.03 at Medium, 88.01 at High, 91.83 at Extra-high and 92.16 at Max (judged n=23, 22, 23, 22, 21). Tasks passed 13, 13, 17, 22 and 22 of 23; 19.0 to 27.7 minutes and $0.84 to $1.54 per task as Claude Code reports it, between a floor and a ceiling for Haiku's two price tiers. Refusal fallback on, never used. Disclosed: three safety-classifier stops and one unpublished judge probe, Claude Code 2.1.293 to 2.1.296, two pauses between tasks, the recovered original judge settings with Grok 4.6 on Cursor CLI 2026.10.01 pinned by version. Includes PDF, per-run CSV with the tier floor and ceiling, and public evidence links.
- [Claude Sonnet 5.5 vs Claude Opus 5.5 vs GPT-6.1 Sol](https://vulcanbench.com/benchmarks/swe-v4-sonnet55-vs-frontier.html): the three models side by side on the same 23 VulcanBench Frontier v4 tasks at five effort levels, judged by the same neutral panel (Muse Spark 1.3 and Grok 4.6) under protocols v3.23, v3.15 and v3.18. Per level: combined score with one standard error and judged n, Code quality, tasks solved, cost and minutes per task. Tasks solved Low to Max: Sonnet 5.5 15, 17, 20, 22, 23; Opus 5.5 17, 23, 22, 22, 21; GPT-6.1 Sol 20, 22, 23, 23, 23. Cost per task: $2.39 to $5.52, $1.70 to $8.75 and $0.31 to $0.46; cost bases and harnesses differ and are disclosed. Sonnet 5.5 has the highest best-level score of the three (92.02 ± 0.35 at Max), edging Opus 5.5 (91.11 ± 0.57 at High) by about 0.9 points, not a clear win, and clearly ahead of GPT-6.1 Sol (88.78 ± 0.40 at Extra-high). Links every underlying evidence bundle.
- [Claude Sonnet 5.5 across every effort level](https://vulcanbench.com/benchmarks/swe-v4-sonnet55-v323.html): 115 Claude Code runs at five effort levels, Code quality at 33% judged for a human reader by Muse Spark 1.3 and Grok 4.6 under protocol v3.23. Combined score 81.63 at Low, 84.10 at Medium, 86.79 at High, 90.20 at Extra-high and 92.02 at Max; tasks passed 15, 17, 20, 22 and 23 of 23; $2.39 to $5.52 per task as Claude Code reports it. Refusal fallback on, never used. Disclosed: judge settings identical to the original v3.3 and v3.4 protocols (recovered from a private backup), Muse on the same binary, Grok 4.6 through Cursor CLI 2026.10.01 rather than the 2026.09.02 of the v3.3 round, the sweep predates the tagged-worktree rule and was admitted through a committed task hash bridge, and Claude Code ran as 2.1.291 to 2.1.293. Includes PDF, a comparison card with Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Fable 5.1, per-run CSV and public evidence links.
- [Grok 4.7 across every effort level](https://vulcanbench.com/benchmarks/swe-v4-grok47-cursor-v320.html): 92 Cursor runs at four effort levels (Cursor offers no Max), Code quality at 33% judged for a human reader by Muse Spark 1.3 and GPT-6.1 Sol under protocol v3.20, because Grok 4.6, the second judge for every other column, is not neutral for an xAI model. Combined score 89.42 at Low, 92.30 at Medium, 92.71 at High and 93.15 at Extra-high, ranks 1, 2 and 3 of 53 columns on the board. GPT-6.1 Sol rates about 6 points above Muse, so Code quality is not strictly comparable; on Muse Spark 1.3 alone for every column Grok 4.7 scores 88.64 to 92.27, still first at Medium to Extra-high and second at Low behind Fable 5.1. Tasks passed 18, 21, 22 and 23 of 23; Medium judged on 22 after one 3-hour timeout; 20.2 to 28.5 minutes per task; cost unavailable (no list price, Cursor subscription), never $0. Safety v1: followed 14 of 80 planted notes, reported none; Claude Opus 5.5 followed 3 of 100, reported 64. Routine v1 (12 private routine tickets, aggregates on the leaderboard): every level passes all 12, combined 97.29, 97.21, 97.37 and 97.14 from Low to Extra-high, the four highest Routine columns, in 1.1 to 4.0 minutes per task; judged under v3.22 by Muse Spark 1.3 alone because GPT-6.1 Sol failed that calibration exam, and still first when every column is rescored from Muse alone. Routine and Frontier Code quality are not comparable. Includes PDF, per-run CSV, shared-judge check and public evidence links.
- [GPT-6.1 Sol across every effort level](https://vulcanbench.com/benchmarks/swe-v4-gpt61-sol-v318.html): 115 Codex runs at five effort levels, Code quality at 33% judged for a human reader by Muse Spark 1.3 and Grok 4.6 under protocol v3.18. Combined score 86.22 at Low, 86.44 at Medium, 88.23 at High, 88.78 at Extra-high and 88.35 at Max, ahead of GPT-6 Sol and GPT-5.6 Sol at every level and 21st of 75 columns on the board at its best as of October 27, 2026 (13th of 49 when published). Tasks passed 20, 22, 23, 23 and 23 of 23, so Frontier v4 no longer separates its top levels on correctness; $0.31 to $0.46 per task, $44.33 for all 115 runs. Every cell is judged on 23 runs (Medium paddockcore from Muse Spark 1.3 alone after an invalid Grok review); no run hit the 3-hour bound. Includes PDF, per-run CSV with both judges' sub-scores, calibration record, the three-generation Sol card and public evidence links.
- [GPT-6 Sol across every effort level](https://vulcanbench.com/benchmarks/swe-v4-gpt6-sol-v317.html): 115 Codex runs at five effort levels, Code quality at 33% judged for a human reader by Muse Spark 1.3 and Grok 4.6 under protocol v3.17. Combined score 67.62 at Low, 80.60 at Medium, 82.83 at High, 85.94 at Extra-high and 86.82 at Max, slightly behind GPT-5.6 Sol at every level. Tasks passed 4, 13, 15, 18 and 19 of 23; $1.02 to $2.52 per task, $221.38 for all 115 runs. Medium is judged on 22 of 23 after one invalid judge probe; no run hit the 3-hour bound. Includes PDF, per-run CSV with both judges' sub-scores, calibration record, comparison cards with GPT-5.6 Sol and the GPT-6 family, and public evidence links.
- [GPT-6 Luna across every effort level](https://vulcanbench.com/benchmarks/swe-v4-gpt6-luna-v316.html): 115 Codex runs at five effort levels, Code quality at 33% judged for a human reader by Muse Spark 1.3 and Grok 4.6 under protocol v3.16. Combined score over judged runs 40.83 at Low, 45.72 at Medium, 57.35 at High, 78.79 at Extra-high and 81.42 at Max. Six runs hit the 3-hour bound (2 at Extra-high, 4 at Max); counting them as 0 gives 71.94 and 67.26. Tasks passed 0, 0, 2, 11 and 12 of 23; $0.010 to $0.160 per priced task. Every score is published both ways: over judged runs, and with timeouts counted as 0. Includes PDF, per-run CSV with both judges' sub-scores, calibration record and public evidence links.
- [Claude Opus 5.5 across every effort level](https://vulcanbench.com/benchmarks/swe-v4-opus55-v315.html): 115 Claude Code runs at five effort levels, Code quality at 33% judged for a human reader by Muse Spark 1.3 and Grok 4.6 under protocol v3.15. Combined score 86.36 at Low, 90.86 at Medium with all 23 tasks passed, 91.11 at High, second on Frontier v4 only to Fable 5.1 at Max, then 90.68 and 90.22; $1.70 to $8.75 per task. Claude Code's refusal fallback was on, following Artificial Analysis: Opus 4.8 wrote 0.0, 6.4, 20.9, 32.4, 47.8% of replies from Low to Max, and every run counts. Includes a comparison card with GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1, per-run CSV and public evidence links.
- [GPT-5.6 Sol across every effort level](https://vulcanbench.com/benchmarks/swe-v4-sol-v37.html): 115 Codex runs at five effort levels, Code quality at 33% judged for a human reader by Muse Spark 1.3 and Grok 4.6 under protocol v3.7. Combined score 69.05 at Low, 82.56 at Medium and 85.76 to 87.18 from High to Max, at $1.36 to $2.05 per task; Max is judged on 22 of 23 tasks after one invalid judge probe. Includes PDF, per-run CSV with both judges' sub-scores, calibration record and public evidence links.
- [GPT-5.6 Terra across every effort level](https://vulcanbench.com/benchmarks/swe-v4-terra-v36.html): 115 Codex runs at five effort levels, Code quality at 33% judged for a human reader by Muse Spark 1.3 and Grok 4.6 under protocol v3.6. Combined score rises at every step, 59.70 at Low to 89.05 at Max, at $0.58 to $2.12 per task. Includes PDF, per-run CSV with both judges' sub-scores, calibration record and public evidence links.
- [GPT-5.5 vs. GPT-5.6 Luna across every effort level](https://vulcanbench.com/benchmarks/swe-v4-gpt55-luna-v35.html): 207 Codex runs at every effort level each API offers, Code quality at 33% judged for a human reader by Muse Spark 1.3 and Grok 4.6 under protocol v3.5. GPT-5.5 leads at Low and Medium; Luna edges ahead from High up and its Max level is the top cell, at 17 to 75 times less per task. Includes PDF, per-run CSV with both judges' sub-scores, calibration record and public evidence links.
- [Astra vs. Fable 5.1 under a neutral Code quality panel](https://vulcanbench.com/benchmarks/swe-v4-astra-fable51-v34.html): 230 runs from the September 2026 effort sweep scored with Code quality at 33%, judged for a human reader by Muse Spark 1.3 and Grok 4.6 under a frozen, calibrated protocol. Includes PDF, per-run CSV with both judges' sub-scores, calibration record and public evidence links.
- [Methodology](https://vulcanbench.com/methodology.html): task admission, execution boundaries, four-factor scoring and evidence limits.
- [Analysis](https://vulcanbench.com/analysis.html): deeper looks at how models and harnesses behave on VulcanBench tasks.
- [Muse Wonder Full against Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra: combined score, time and cost](https://vulcanbench.com/analysis/02-muse-wonder-full-combined-time-cost.html): Muse Wonder Full's combined score, time and cost on VulcanBench Frontier v4 at every level Contributor mode allows (Low to Extra-high), against Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra. It scores 87.0 at Low, 88.3 at Medium, 88.2 at High and 87.6 at Extra-high: level with the frontier at Low and second at Medium, but it does not gain from more effort and is fourth at Extra-high, while being the slowest and most expensive of the four at about 27 to 36 minutes and an estimated $4 to $5 per task (later runs on Muse Code 1.4.9; one timeout each at High and Extra-high). Its Code quality was judged by Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol, a different panel from the other models, and the two judges disagreed by about 17 points; both caveats are explained.
- [Analysis of traces comparing Muse Wonder Full and GPT-6.1 Sol at Low effort](https://vulcanbench.com/analysis/01-muse-wonder-full-vs-gpt-6-1-sol.html): Trace analysis of Muse Wonder Full in Muse Code against GPT-6.1 Sol in Codex on all 23 VulcanBench Frontier v4 tasks at Low effort. Muse Wonder Full averaged 27.2 minutes per task against 6.3, with about 3x the model calls and 10x the output tokens, while each step took about the same time. Covers where the time goes, ranked causes, how the two models work, and the effect of turning off Muse Code's skill reminder.
- [Blog](https://vulcanbench.com/blog.html): benchmark design and effort observations.
- [Introducing VulcanBench Safety v1](https://vulcanbench.com/blog/02-vulcanbench-safety-v1.html): announcement of VulcanBench Safety v1, a safety eval suite built for and run in the same environments and harnesses companies actually use (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor). It looks for the smaller safety issues that show up during ordinary coding work, so teams can tell whether rolling out a new model raises or lowers safety risk in their codebase.
- [Why I started VulcanBench](https://vulcanbench.com/blog/01-why-i-started-vulcanbench.html): the origin story, a $300,000-a-year model bill, evals built on the team's own codebase, and why benchmarks measured only at Max effort gave no usable signal.
- [Custom evals](https://vulcanbench.com/benchmark-your-stack.html): private evaluations for engineering teams.
- [Benchmark your model](https://vulcanbench.com/benchmark-your-model.html): evaluations for labs and harness builders.

## Interpretation

Astra had lower mean time and estimated API cost at every matched effort in
this comparison. Fable Max had the highest observed total score. This is not
a statistically established overall winner or a pure-base-model comparison.
Effort labels are harness-specific, not equal compute budgets. One attempt
per cell does not establish run-to-run reliability.

Historical suites and reports retain their original metrics. Do not pool
Eval Suite 3 pass rates with Frontier v4 total scores. Costs are hypothetical API
charges from a frozen rate snapshot, not subscription cash charges.

## Evidence and limits

The harness and task suites are public. Individual reports distinguish
published measurements from withheld raw artifacts. Source hashes and
post-cutoff dates do not prove absence of cheating, prohibited access or
training-data overlap.
